key_insight: The paper proves a new upper bound on the dimension of simple connected GHZ graphs in terms of vertex connectivity: at most 2^(κ(G)-1) + C(κ(G),2).
engineering_relevance: This gives quantum optics and distributed quantum computing a graph-theoretic limit on how large a GHZ state can be generated from a given connectivity structure.
method: Translate GHZ photonic experiments into edge-coloured, edge-weighted graphs.
Bound the number of feasible monochromatic inherited vertex colourings using graph connectivity parameters.
Derive additional bounds using edge connectivity and maximum degree.
evidence_signal: The result is theoretical and extends prior proofs for graphs with vertex connectivity at most 2, tightening the known limits from the abstract.
watch_item: The bound is only for simple connected GHZ graphs, so it may not directly cover more general experimental graph constructions or weighted/irregular variants.
